title: Win the specificity war
summary: The current-page link should be orange and bold, but an id selector keeps winning.
brief: The "Docs" link has the class current, and the .current rule makes it orange (#ea580c) and bold (700). But it shows grey and regular like the others.
Make it orange and bold by adding one new rule. Do not edit or delete the existing rules, and do not use !important.
hints: Inspect the link: two rules set its colour. Which one is more specific?
#site-nav a contains an id. One id outweighs any number of classes, so .current, even placed later, cannot win.
Write a selector with the same id plus the class: #site-nav .current. It beats #site-nav a (an id and a class versus an id and an element).
solutionNotes: Specificity is compared column by column: ids, then classes (and attributes and pseudo-classes), then elements. #site-nav a is (1, 0, 1); .current is (0, 1, 0), so it loses however late it appears. #site-nav .current is (1, 1, 0), which beats (1, 0, 1). The lasting lesson: ids in selectors make styles hard to override, which is why most style guides avoid them.
